answer: Profit-dominant bonding resists sybils: each identity locks a refundable deposit sized to exceed the maximum value any single identity could extract by cheating, so fraud is never net-positive. An attacker spinning up a lotus-field of fakes must fund that full deposit per head — there is no shared nectar of cheap reputation — and since the catchable gain per identity is capped below its own bond, every fake stands to burn more than it can steal. One honest identity earns its deposit back like a steady ember; a farm pays N separate bonds to chase a payoff each bond already outweighs.
